source.snippet: I have a new client with an existing website. She has been using Google Ad Manager successfully for several years, except for one issue: she would like all third party ads removed. That is, she would like to direct sell ad space on the site to local companies only. I have spent a couple of unsuccessful hours trying to find a way to turn off the ads from other agencies/3rd parties. My searches provide conflicting information.

problem_statement: Web consultants and small publishers want to configure Google Ad Manager for direct-sold local advertising only, but GAM's UI and documentation make it difficult to reliably block all programmatic/3rd-party demand, costing billable hours and delaying client launches.
target_segment: Freelance web consultants and small independent publishers managing ad operations for local business clients.
notes: Consultant is on a paid client engagement — time wasted is directly billable cost. A step-by-step GAM configuration guide or a lightweight SaaS that audits and enforces direct-only ad rules could sell to this segment. Single signal but professional context elevates relevance.
